- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.6) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.2) in recent days, model tends to overpredict; reduce forecast to avoid overreaction.  
- Model consistently overestimates prices after sharp upward spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 3–5 days); apply a 1–2 day lag correction or cap forecast at 1–2% above peak.  
- Model underestimates mean-reversion periods (e.g., after 70+ price levels); add 0.5–1.5% upward bias if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum (last 5–7 days of true outcome); adjust forecast to reflect sentiment shift in final 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.4 → -0.2 → +0.6), model tends to lag; apply 1–2 day lead correction to anticipate sentiment shift.
